academics.personalStatement:
“Don’t stop there; there lies so much more potential in you,” said my teacher, who helped me to build something I dreamt of in my childhood. That teacher is Dr. Iqbal Murtza, who led my two years of Final Year Project (FYP) journey. After the completion of my FYP, he told me that I should pursue higher studies and delve deeper into it. To which I asked, what are your respectable suggestions? There, he told me about South Korea and the research orientations that they possess. From then on, I began to explore research areas in South Korea and found my career direction. The thing that inspires me about South Korea is their keenness in innovation, research, and their culture – peeked through the window of his professional social media profile – especially in the area I’m motivated in: Computer Science and Engineering, Software Engineering, and Computing Frameworks.

A curious child who had a computer in his house since his early life and who used to spend a significant portion of his day messing around with the computer. That child was me. Hi, I’m Ahmad Hassan, from Islamabad, Pakistan. I’m 22 years old and currently at the end of my bachelor’s degree in software engineering at Air University, Pakistan, and am a topper of my batch. Since the beginning of my life, I have been interested in computers. The major reason for it was where I grew up. Our home was in the tech market, so I had early familiarity with the ongoing tech.

The inciting incident was when my father asked, “Can we utilize all our phones to run your game?” to which I answered, “No,” but the inner skeptic was never satisfied. Since then, I have kept my curiosity fueled by my father’s question. This question became a catalyst in finding my passion and place in life. I became determined to pursue a pathway that can make this possible. All of this led me to where I am, doing software engineering at one of the top universities of our country’s capital, Air University, Islamabad. There, I grasped the core concepts and fundamentals of software engineering, achieving honors (A) grades throughout my degree.

While the offered curriculum was supposed to fulfill my hunger to learn more, I was always leaning towards what new can be invented, the latest trends, and future technologies. For this, I volunteered as a junior trainee researcher under Dr. Azhar Imran Mudassir (Shenzhen University, China). There, I learned the ethics of academics and research and contributed to several papers, getting my name into notable research articles. I worked on CNN-based architectures for medicinal plant disease detection, achieving 97% accuracy using transfer learning techniques. This work strengthened my understanding of model optimization, dataset curation, performance evaluation metrics, and experimental reproducibility. Moreover, I contributed to a comprehensive review of machine and deep learning methods for coronary artery stenosis diagnosis, where I designed system architectures and experimental pipelines for the segmentation and classification workflows.

Parallel to all, I continued my research journey in experimental ideas in human–computer interaction, which reflected my interdisciplinary curiosity. As the first author of the manuscript “Keyboard Evaluation Framework,” I developed a structured narrative framework analyzing keyboard evolution, ergonomic optimization, and interaction design paradigms. This experience connected me to the research world and its respective principles.

Then came the time that I awaited the most: to choose my final year project. I chose my final year project, “Fractal: A Decentralized Computation Harvesting Framework,” which brought my father’s vision to reality. I designed, implemented, and developed a distributed machine learning framework (my FYP) under the supervision of Dr. Iqbal Murtza – post-doctorate from South Korea – which focused on federated learning and mobile-centric distributed systems. I engineered a client-server architecture that aggregates computational resources from edge devices while implementing device-aware resource profiling (battery, memory, and network constraints) for efficient orchestration. This project strengthened my skills in TensorFlow, TensorFlow Lite, and scalable system design, and further solidified my interest in decentralized AI infrastructures. Dr. Iqbal Murtza is one of the pioneers in making me seize the opportunity to pursue higher education.

The intuition of pursuing international studies is the opportunities of attending up-to-date conferences, learning about new markets and academic trends, and research directions. For the next phase of my life, I want to be a master’s student at prestigious universities in South Korea, working on distributed computation, federated learning, advanced AI systems, scalable machine learning systems, efficient distributed architectures, and intelligent edge computing frameworks, which aligns with my future study direction.

Aside from academics, I’m a hobbyist. I write poems, quotes, short stories, and essays in both English and Urdu. I have won 2 competitions: one for short story writing and the other for academic technical writing. I possess a keen sense of aesthetics, which helps me express emotional abstractions and perfection through the art of digital design and photography. I also enjoy music and its production. I have written lyrics that convey deep meanings and are written with respect to Shakespeare's poetic meter. I sang those lyrics on the beats by me and produced 4 songs. I love playing with circuits and making projects with Arduino. It is my passion to relate, get information, and connect dots for a concept into interdisciplinary mediums. Relating concepts around different subjects and finding a universal pattern satisfies my journey of fulfilling curiosities remarkably.

By achieving my goal of getting my master’s degree under the roof of prestigious Korean institutions, I will strive to bring academic success and innovation, and contribute to the R&D domain of research and advances in federated learning, computer vision, decentralized AI, and high-performance learning systems with real-world societal impact.
academics.studyPlan:
Language Study Plan

Long before I applied for this GKS scholarship, I started to learn Korean on my own through YouTube and Duolingo. These platforms helped me to understand and learn the basic level of Korean, from which I will be able to communicate with natives at a beginner level.

My Korean language journey started by watching movies; I saw my first Korean movie named “The Parasite 2019.” I saw that in the Korean language and got familiar with common terminologies. I got to know about the director Bong Joon Ho and watched his other movies – most of them in the Korean language – including “Mother, 2009.” This sparked the spirit in me to watch more Korean movies – not knowing it would be a catalyst for me to learn Korean. I get to know about the cities of Korea by watching “OldBoy, 2003,” “Train to Busan, 2016,” and many more movies like that. This ignited the spirit in me to learn and explore Korean more. Moreover, Korean bands like BTS and Blackpink helped me to correct my pronunciation, making it sound native.

Now that I’m applying for GKS, learning Korean for a year will be a huge benefit for me. By learning Korean, I will be able to not just communicate and interact but also understand their culture, work in Korean tech companies, and seize the opportunities that Korean speakers exclusively can. I will be able to understand Korean technical papers and comprehend their talks and conferences at an advanced level. Therefore, I am willing to get this prestigious opportunity to learn the Korean language.

Even after the Korean language course, I will continue to learn it by attending events organized by the university. Talking to Korean friends in their language will be a proud moment for me. Over time, I will keep expanding my vocabulary, focus on pronunciation, and devote a significant portion of my time to reading, writing, and speaking Korean to prepare myself to pass the TOPIK-II level 5-6. Getting the Korean language at the professional level on my curriculum vitae (CV) will be an honor for me, signifying my dedication and respect for Korea.

Goal of study & Study Plan

I’m Ahmad Hassan, a student of Software Engineering (bachelor’s). Throughout my degree, I have delved into the fundamentals of software engineering and computer science disciplines. As a software engineer, I have learned to look at things with a perspective of problem-solving and coding as a powerful tool to implement those solutions. The orientation of my degree was particularly about the design and architectural problems and the ethics of software. Courses like Agent-based Software Engineering, Natural Language Processing, and Operating Systems helped me to grasp the AI and distributed computing concepts, which then became an integral part of my future research journey.

My interest as a researcher falls under federated learning (FL), distributed computation, advanced AI systems, scalable machine learning systems, on-device training, efficient distributed architectures, and intelligent edge computing frameworks. What drives me the most is the innovation and the new ways this methodology can unlock. As AI requires extensive resources to operate, we can devise and invent new ways that can increase the efficiency of these systems, unlocking a new era of computing. This level of efficiency can be achieved via two factors: the algorithms and the machines themselves. The area I want to research and am interested in focuses on both, mainly on how to distribute the workload across the globe, on specialized devices, or on ordinary edge devices, making the newer technologies accessible to everyone, shifting the operational AI paradigm to handheld devices. Therefore, I’m applying for the Computer Science and Engineering Program for my master's program.

For the preparation of this program, I have built an implementation of federated learning and devised a new federated framework named “Fractal: A Decentralized Computation Harvesting Framework."

This project was prepared under the supervision of Dr. Iqbal Murtza (post-doc, Korea). I engineered a client–server architecture that aggregates computational resources from edge devices while implementing device-aware resource profiling (battery, memory, and network constraints) for efficient orchestration. This project strengthened my skills in TensorFlow, TensorFlow Lite, and scalable system design, and further solidified my interest in decentralized AI infrastructures. The Fractal framework focuses on harvesting resources from the mobile edge devices to train not just the federated compatible models but also huge machine learning and deep learning models, which will contribute to implementing and testing out innovative high-scale models that could not be previously implemented due to the inaccessibility of such huge computing infrastructure.

Moreover, to get myself familiarized with the academic and research world, I got myself appointed as a junior trainee researcher under Dr. Azhar Imran Mudassir (Shenzhen University, China). There, I learned the ethics of academics and research and contributed to several papers, getting my name into notable research articles. While securing an A grade in courses like Probability and Statistics, Stochastic Processes, Agent-Based SE, and NLP, I grasped the foundational concepts and contributed to innovation towards the integration of AI. I worked on CNN-based architectures for medicinal plant disease detection, achieving 97% accuracy using transfer learning techniques. This work strengthened my understanding of model optimization, dataset curation, performance evaluation metrics, and experimental reproducibility. Moreover, I contributed to a comprehensive review of machine and deep learning methods for coronary artery stenosis diagnosis, where I designed system architectures and experimental pipelines for segmentation and classification workflows. Parallel to all, I continued my research in human–computer interaction, which reflects my interdisciplinary curiosity. As the first author of a manuscript, I developed a structured narrative framework analyzing keyboard evolution, ergonomic optimization, and interaction design paradigms. These experiences provided me with the expertise to enter the academic world.

My Bachelor’s in Software Engineering is ending in the upcoming months, sooner than the GKS start of classes phase. I want to further pursue my career in Computer Science and the Software Engineering domain. I aim to delve deeper into the core fundamentals of the courses I have read in my bachelor’s curriculum, so I will get updated on the latest research trends and present my contributions to it. I consider myself a highly motivated, curious, disciplined, and hardworking student, which proves me to be the most fitting candidate for your prestigious institute. I am strongly confident that the international academic and research-intensive nature of the Global Korea Scholarship 2026 will provide the intellectual rigor and collaborative ecosystem necessary to excel and pursue my research vision.
academics.futurePlanAfterStudy: The plans after graduation from the master’s program include either pursuing a Ph.D. in the domain of Computer Science in Korea or seeking a job there as an R&D researcher or an AI/software expert and engineer. With expertise in the Korean language and prominent research work from your prestigious university, I will have the freedom to either step into the Korean tech market, go back to my home country, or pursue further higher education. I present my special thanks to my teachers for helping me define my ambition plan and to you for your time and consideration.
